x: Commentary on the sura "al-Mulk" (Dominion). In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Blessed is He in whose hand is dominion, and He is over all things competent (1) [He] who created death and life to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed — and He is the Exalted in Might, the Forgiving (2)
By His saying, Exalted is His mention,
h
Blessed (tabāraka)
He means: He is magnified and exalted;
h
He in whose hand is dominion
: in His hand are the dominion of this world and the Hereafter and their sovereignty; His command and decree are effective in both;
h
and He is over all things competent
. He says: He is able to do whatever He wills to do; nothing prevents Him from doing it, and no incapacity comes between Him and it.
His saying:
h
[He] who created death and life
: so He causes whom He wills and whatever He wills to die, and gives life to whom He wills and whatever He wills until a known term,
h
to test you [as to] which of you is best in deed
. He says: to try you and see which of you, O people, is more obedient to Him and quicker in seeking His good pleasure.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told me, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda
m: . He said: God humbled the son of Adam with death, and made this world an abode of life and an abode of passing away, and made the Hereafter an abode of recompense and permanence

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: [He] who created death and life to test you
: It is mentioned that the Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: "God has humbled the son of Adam with death"

x: His saying:
h
and He is the Exalted in Might
. He says: He is the strong, severe in vengeance upon whoever disobeys Him and opposes His command,
h
the Forgiving
of the sins of whoever turns to Him and repents of his sins.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

[He] who created seven heavens in layers. You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency; so return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any breaks? (3) Then return [your] vision twice again. [Your] vision will return to you humbled while it is fatigued (4)
The Exalted says, informing of His attribute:
h
[He] who created seven heavens in layers (ṭibāqan)
, layer upon layer, one above another.
His saying:
h
You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency
you do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful, in what He created — not in heaven nor in earth nor elsewhere —
h
any inconsistency (tafāwut)
He means: any discrepancy.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: You do not see in the creation of the Most Merciful any inconsistency
: you do not see in them any discrepancy.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda

x: The reciters differed over the reading of that. The general body of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, read:
h
min tafāwut
with an alif
n
. The general body of the reciters of Kufa read it: (min tafawwut) with doubling of the wāw and without an alif
n
. The correct view on this is that they are two well-known readings with one meaning, as it was said:
h
and do not turn [your cheek] (tuṣaʿʿir)
and (lā tuṣāʿir)
n
; and "I looked after so-and-so" (taʿahhadtu) and taʿāhadtuhu, and "I purified myself" (taṭahhartu) and taẓāhartu; and likewise tafāwut and tafawwut.

evidence.text: The reciters differed over the reading of that.
The general body of the reciters of Medina and Basra, and some of the Kufans, read: {min tafāwut} with an alif (1).
The general body of the reciters of Kufa read it: (min tafawwut) with doubling of the wāw and without an alif (2).

x: His saying:
h
so return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any breaks (fuṭūr)?
. He says: so turn the eye back; do you see in it any cracks and fissures
n
? This is from God's saying:
h
The heavens almost rupture (yatafaṭṭarna) from above them
[al-Shūrā: 5], meaning: they split and crack. And "al-fuṭūr" is the verbal noun of faṭara, fuṭūran.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: . He said: The fuṭūr is the fissures

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: . He says: do you see any flaw, O son of Adam.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:
Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān:

x: His saying:
h
Then return [your] vision twice again
. Mighty is His praise says: then turn the eye back, O son of Adam, twice — time after time — and look whether you see any breaks or inconsistency;
h
twice again, [your] vision will return to you humbled (khāsiʾan)
. He says: your sight will return to you abased and driven off, from their saying to the dog: ikhsaʾ, when they drive it away, that is: be gone, abased;
h
while it is fatigued (ḥasīr)
. He says: it is worn out and weary.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās:
m: . He says: do you see any flaw in the sky;
[your] vision will return to you humbled while it is fatigued
through the darkness of the night.

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās

x: His saying:
h
while it is fatigued (ḥasīr)
. He says: murjif — faint and quaking
n

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: [Your] vision will return to you humbled (khāsiʾan)

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda
m: . He says: worn out, having seen no flaw or inconsistency

x: Some of them said: khāsiʾ and ḥasīr are one.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: so return [your] vision [to the sky]; do you see any breaks?

— the verse. He said: The khāsiʾ and the ḥāsir are one; its gaze is exhausted from seeing any rupture in it, so it returns exhausted before it has seen any rupture in it. He said: But when the Day of Resurrection comes, it will be ruptured and then split, and then a greater matter than that will come: it will be stripped away.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with lamps and have made [from] them what is thrown at the devils and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze (5)
The Exalted says:
h
And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with lamps
, and they are the stars; He made them lamps because of their giving light. So too the dawn (ṣubḥ) is called ṣubḥ for the light that shines for people from the day;
h
and have made [from] them what is thrown at the devils
. He says: and We made the lamps with which We beautified the nearest heaven things to be hurled at the devils: they are stoned with them.

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
m: And We have certainly beautified the nearest heaven with lamps and have made [from] them what is thrown at the devils

: God, Mighty is His praise, created these stars only for three purposes: He created them as an adornment for the nearest heaven, as missiles for the devils, and as signs by which one is guided; so whoever interprets them as anything else has spoken by his own opinion, erred in his portion, lost his share, and burdened himself with what he has no knowledge of

x: His saying:
h
and have prepared for them the punishment of the Blaze
. Mighty is His praise says: and We have prepared for the devils in the Hereafter the punishment of the Blaze, which will be stoked against them and set alight.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
And for those who disbelieve in their Lord is the punishment of Hell, and wretched is the destination (6) When they are thrown into it, they hear from it a [terrible] inhaling while it boils up (7)
The Exalted says:
h
And for those who disbelieve in their Lord
who created them in this world,
h
is the punishment of Hell
in the Hereafter,
h
and wretched is the destination
. He says: and wretched is the destination, the punishment of Hell.
His saying:
h
When they are thrown into it
. He means: when the disbelievers are thrown into Hell,
h
they hear from it
— he means from Hell —
h
a [terrible] inhaling (shahīq)
. By shahīq he means the sound that comes out of the chest with force, like the sound of the donkey, as Ruʾba said in describing a donkey
n
He rattled in the chest, a [harsh] braying, or gasped (shahaq),
until it was said: a brayer — and he had not brayed
His saying:
h
while it boils up (tafūr)
. He says: [and it]
n
seethes.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Mujāhid:
m: they hear from it a [terrible] inhaling while it boils up
. He says: it seethes as a cooking pot seethes

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

It almost bursts with rage. Every time a company is thrown into it, its keepers ask them, "Did there not come to you a warner?" (8) They will say, "Yes, a warner had come to us, but we denied and said, 'God has not sent down anything. You are not but in great error'" (9)
The Exalted says: Hell almost
h
bursts
. He says: it is torn apart and cut to pieces out of rage at its inhabitants.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: . He says: it is torn apart

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: : parts of it almost separate from other parts, and it splits open

x: I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say:

c: ʿUbayd told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
. He says: it is torn apart

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: . He said: Bursting (tamayyuz) is being torn apart in rage against those who disobey God, in anger for God and in vengeance for Him (2).

x: His saying:
h
Every time a company is thrown into it
. Mighty is His praise says: every time a group is thrown into Hell,
h
its keepers ask them, "Did there not come to you a warner?"
He says: the keepers of Hell ask the company, saying to them: Did there not come to you in the world a warner who warned you of this punishment you are in? And the wretched ones answer them and say:
h
Yes, a warner had come to us
warning us of this, but we denied him and said to him:
h
God has not sent down anything. You are not but in great error
. He says: in a deviation from the truth that is far.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

And they will say, "If only we had been listening or reasoning, we would not be among the companions of the Blaze" (10) And they will admit their sin, so [it is] alienation for the companions of the Blaze (11)
The Exalted says: and the company that was thrown into the Fire said to the keepers:
h
If only we had been
in the world
h
listening or reasoning
of the warners, of the counsel they brought us, or understanding from them what they were calling us to,
h
we would not be today among the companions of the Blaze
. He means the people of the Fire.
His saying:
h
And they will admit their sin

. He says: so they acknowledged their sin. He put "sin" in the singular though it is added to a plural, because it has the sense of an act, so the singular stands for the whole, as one says: the people's stipend came out, and the people's gifts.
h
so [it is] alienation for the companions of the Blaze
. He says: so distance for the people of the Fire.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: so [it is] alienation for the companions of the Blaze

c: Ibn Ḥumayd told us, he said: Mihrān told us, from Sufyān, from Salama b.
m: so [it is] alienation for the companions of the Blaze
. He said: Suḥq is a valley in Hell

x: The reciters read it with lightening of the ḥāʾ from "al-suḥq", and that is the correct view in our opinion, because that is the eloquent usage of the Arabs; and some of the Arabs vocalize it with ḍamma
n

evidence.text: The reciters read it with lightening of the ḥāʾ from "al-suḥq", and that is the correct view in our opinion, because that is the eloquent usage of the Arabs; and some of the Arabs vocalize it with ḍamma (3).

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Indeed, those who fear their Lord unseen will have forgiveness and great reward (12) And conceal your speech or publicize it; indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts (13)
The Exalted says: those who fear their Lord unseen. He says: though they have not seen Him,
h
will have forgiveness
. He says: they will have pardon from God for their sins,
h
and great reward
. He says: and an ample recompense from God for their fearing Him unseen.
His saying:
h
And conceal your speech or publicize it
. Mighty is His praise says: and hide your speech and your talk, O people, or make it public and manifest,
h
indeed, He is Knowing of that within the breasts

. He says: He has knowledge of the secret thoughts of the breasts that have not been spoken; so how of what has been uttered and spoken, whether hidden or made public? For whoever is not hidden from by the secrets of breasts, other things are all the more certain not to be hidden from Him.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Does He who created not know, while He is the Subtle, the Aware? (14) It is He who made the earth tame for you — so walk among its slopes and eat of His provision — and to Him is the resurrection (15)
The Exalted says: Does the Lord, Mighty is His praise, not know
h
He who created
, that is, whom He created? He says: how could His creation that He created be hidden from Him,
h
while He is the Subtle
toward His servants,
h
the Aware
of them and of their deeds.
His saying:
h
It is He who made the earth tame for you
. The Exalted says: God is He who made the earth tame for you, easy, and made it smooth for you,
h
so walk among its slopes (manākib)
The people of knowledge differed over the meaning of
h
manākibihā
Some of them said: its manākib are its mountains.
Mention of those who said that:

c: ʿAlī told me, he said: Abū Ṣāliḥ told us, he said: Muʿāwiya related to me, from ʿAlī, from Ibn ʿAbbās
Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda, from Bashīr b.
m: Kaʿb, that he recited this verse:

. He said to a slave girl of his: If you know what its manākib are, you are free for the sake of God. She said: Its manākib are its mountains. It was as if he had been struck across the face, and he regretted [losing] his slave girl, and he asked; some of them told him to go ahead, and some forbade him, so he asked Abū l-Dardāʾ, who said: Good is in tranquility, and evil is in doubt, so leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt

c: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: Muʿādh b. Hishām told us, he said: My father related to me, from Qatāda, from Bashīr b.
Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda:
Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda

x: Others said:
h
manākibihā
means: its edges and regions.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: . He says: walk in its edges

c: Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Saʿīd, from Qatāda,
m: that Bashīr b. Kaʿb al-ʿAdawī recited this verse:

and said to his slave girl: If you tell me what its manākib are, you are free. She said: Its regions. He wanted to marry her, so he asked Abū l-Dardāʾ, who said: Good is in tranquility, and evil is in doubt, so leave what makes you doubt for what does not make you doubt.

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
. He said: its roads and passes

x: The sounder of the two views, in my opinion, is the view of those who said: the meaning of that is: walk in its regions and sides. That is because its regions are the equivalent of the human being's manākib (shoulders), which are among his extremities.

evidence.text: Ibn Bashshār told us, he said: ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda, from Bashīr b. Kaʿb, that he recited this verse: {so walk among its slopes}.

Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Saʿīd, from Qatāda, that Bashīr b. Kaʿb al-ʿAdawī recited this verse: {so walk among its slopes} and said to his slave girl: If you tell me what its manākib are, you are free.

x: His saying:
h
and eat of His provision
. He says: and eat of God's provision that He brought out for you from the slopes of the earth,
h
and to Him is the resurrection
. The Exalted says: and to God is your being raised from your graves.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Do you feel secure that He who [holds authority] in the heaven will not cause the earth to swallow you while it shakes? (16) Or do you feel secure that He who [holds authority] in the heaven will not send against you a storm of stones? Then you will know how [severe] was My warning (17)
The Exalted says:
h
Do you feel secure that He who [holds authority] in the heaven
, O disbelievers,
h
will not cause the earth to swallow you while it shakes?
. He says: and behold, the earth is going to and fro with you and convulsing;
h
Or do you feel secure that He who [holds authority] in the heaven
— and He is God —
h
will not send against you a storm of stones (ḥāṣib)
, and it is dust in which there are small pebbles (ḥaṣbāʾ),
h
then you will know how [severe] was My warning
. He says: you will know, O disbelievers, how the outcome of My warning to you was, when you denied it and rejected it against My messenger.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

And already those before them denied, and how [terrible] was My reproach (18) Do they not see the birds above them with wings outspread and [sometimes] folded in? None holds them up except the Most Merciful. Indeed He is, of all things, Seeing (19)
The Exalted says: those who came before these polytheists of Quraysh, of the bygone nations, denied their messengers,
h
and how [terrible] was My reproach
. He says: how was My reproach of their denial of them?
h
Do they not see the birds above them with wings outspread
. He says: do these polytheists not see the birds above them spreading their wings?
h
and [sometimes] folded in
. He says: and they fold in their wings at times? What is meant by that is that they spread their wings at times, and fold them at times.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda
m: . He said: The bird spreads its wing as you have seen, then folds it

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
with wings outspread and [sometimes] folded in
: their extending their wings and their folding them

x: His saying:
h
None holds them up except the Most Merciful

. He says: nothing holds the birds that spread their wings above you except the Most Merciful. He says: so in that they have a reminder if they would take heed, and a lesson if they would take warning, by which they may know that their Lord is one, with no partner,
h
indeed He is, of all things, Seeing
. He says: God is, of everything, possessed of sight and awareness; no flaw enters His management, and no inconsistency is seen in His creation.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Or who is it that could be an army for you to aid you other than the Most Merciful? The disbelievers are not but in delusion (20)

The Exalted says to the polytheists of Quraysh who associate others with Him: who is this who is an army for you, O disbelievers in Him, to aid you besides the Most Merciful if He intends evil for you, so as to ward off from you what He intended for you of that?
h
The disbelievers are not but in delusion
. The Exalted says: the disbelievers in God are only in delusion in their thinking that their gods will bring them near to God in nearness, and that they can benefit or harm.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Or who is it that could provide for you if He withheld His provision? But they have persisted in insolence and aversion (21)
The Exalted says: who is this who feeds you and gives you drink and brings you your sustenance if your Lord withheld from you His provision with which He provides you?
His saying:
h
But they have persisted in insolence and aversion
. He says: rather, they have persisted in transgression, aversion from the truth and arrogance.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: But they have persisted in insolence and aversion

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding God's saying:
But they have persisted in insolence and aversion

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Then is he who walks fallen on his face better guided or he who walks upright on a straight path? (22)
The Exalted says:
h
Then is he who walks
, O people,
h
fallen on his face
, not seeing what is before him or to his right or his left,
h
better guided
. He says: more upright on the road and better guided to it,
h
or he who walks upright
with the walk of the children of Adam on his feet,
h
on a straight path
. He says: on a road with no crookedness in it. It was said:
h
mukibban
, because it is an intransitive verb, and when it is not transitive they put an alif in it, saying: akabba so-and-so ʿalā wajhihi, and he is mukibb. From it is the saying of al-Aʿshā
n
Bowed (mukibban) over its two horns
n
, digging at its root,
on the back of a plain bare of tracks, a loose sandy waste
n
So he said mukibban because it is an intransitive verb; and when it is transitive, the alif is dropped from it, so it is said: kababtu so-and-so ʿalā wajhihi, and God cast him (kabbahu) on his face.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: Then is he who walks fallen on his face better guided or he who walks upright on a straight path?
. He says: is he who walks in error better guided, or he who walks rightly guided?

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
or he who walks upright on a straight path

x: I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say:

c: ʿUbayd told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
Then is he who walks fallen on his face
better guided or he who walks upright
, the believer? God gave a parable of the two.

x: Others said: Rather, what is meant by that is that God will gather the disbeliever on the Day of Resurrection on his face. So He said:
h
Then is he who walks fallen on his face
on the Day of Resurrection better guided, or he who walks upright on that day?
Mention of those who said that:

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: Then is he who walks fallen on his face better guided

: He is the disbeliever, who was devoted to disobeying God in this world; God will gather him on the Day of Resurrection on his face. It was said: O Prophet of God, how will the disbeliever be gathered on his face? He said: “The One who made him walk on his two feet is able to gather him on the Day of Resurrection on his face.”

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:
m: Then is he who walks fallen on his face

. He said: He is the disbeliever who acts in disobedience to God, and God will gather him on the Day of Resurrection on his face. Maʿmar said: It was said to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: How will they walk on their faces? He said: "The One who made them walk on their feet is able to make them walk on their faces"

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:
m: he who walks upright on a straight path
. He said: The believer, who acted in obedience to God; God will gather him upon his obedience (1).

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Say, "It is He who has produced you and made for you hearing and vision and hearts; little are you grateful" (23)
The Exalted says: say, O Muḥammad, to those polytheists who deny the resurrection: God is He who brought you into being and created you,
h
and made for you hearing
with which you hear,
h
and vision
with which you see,
h
and hearts
with which you reason;
h
little are you grateful
. He says: little do you thank your Lord for these favors
n
that He has bestowed upon you.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Say, "It is He who has multiplied you throughout the earth, and to Him you will be gathered" (24) And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?" (25)
The Exalted says to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: say, O Muḥammad: God is
h
He who has multiplied you throughout the earth
. He says: God is He who created you on the earth,
h
and to Him you will be gathered
. He says: and to God you will be gathered, being assembled from your graves for the place of reckoning,
h
And they say, "When is this promise, if you should be truthful?"
. Mighty is His praise says: and the polytheists say: when will come what you promise us of the gathering to God, if you are truthful in your promise to us of what you promise us?
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h

Say, "The knowledge is only with God, and I am only a clear warner" (26) But when they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieve will be distressed, and it will be said, "This is that for which you used to call" (27)

The Exalted says to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: say, O Muḥammad, to these people who hasten you to bring on the punishment and the establishment of the Hour: the knowledge of the Hour, and of when the Resurrection will come, is only with God; none other knows it,
h
and I am only a clear warner
. He says: I am only a warner to you, warning you of God's punishment for your disbelief in Him,
h
clear
: one who has made his warning plain to you.
His saying:
h
But when they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieve will be distressed
. The Exalted says: when these polytheists saw God's punishment
h
approaching (zulfa)
. He says: near, and witnessed it,
h
the faces of those who disbelieve will be distressed
. He says: God will make the faces of the disbelievers grieved by that.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on His saying
h
zulfa
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yaʿqūb b. Ibrāhīm told me, he said: Ibn ʿUlayya told us, from Abū Rajāʾ, from al-Ḥasan
m: But when they see it approaching
. He said: when they witnessed it

c: Ibn al-Muthannā told us, he said: Yaḥyā b. Abī Bukayr told us, he said: Shuʿba told us, from Abū Rajāʾ, he said:
m: I asked al-Ḥasan about His saying:
But when they see it approaching

c: Muḥammad b. ʿAmr told me, he said: Abū ʿĀṣim told us, he said: ʿĪsā told us; and al-Ḥārith told me, he said: al-Ḥasan told us, he said: Waraqāʾ told us,
m: both from Ibn Abī Najīḥ, from Mujāhid regarding His saying:
But when they see it approaching
. He said: it has drawn near

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: But when they see it approaching, the faces of those who disbelieve will be distressed
: at what they witnessed of God's punishment.

c: Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā told us, he said: Ibn Thawr told us, from Maʿmar, from Qatāda:
m: But when they see it approaching
. He said: when they see God's punishment close at hand. He says: their faces were distressed when they witnessed of God's punishment and disgrace what they witnessed

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: But when they see it approaching
. It was said: zulfa is present; God's punishment, Mighty and Majestic, was present before them

x: h
and it will be said, "This is that for which you used to call"
. He says: and God said to them: this is the punishment which you used to ask your Lord to hasten for you.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Yūnus told me, he said: Ibn Wahb informed us, he said: Ibn Zayd said
m: and it will be said “This is that for which you used to call"
. He said: their demanding the punishment be hastened.

x: The reciters differed over the reading of that. The general body of the reciters of the major cities read it:
h
taddaʿūn
with doubling of the dāl, meaning: taftaʿilūn ("you claim/call for"), from duʿāʾ. And it is reported from Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk that they read it: (tadʿūn), meaning: you do [it] in this world
n

c: Aḥmad b. Yūsuf told me, he said: al-Qāsim told us, he said: Ḥajjāj told us, from Hārūn, he said: Abān al-ʿAṭṭār and Saʿīd b. Abī ʿArūba informed us, from Qatāda,
m: that he read it: (alladhī kuntum bihi tadʿūn) lightened, and said: They used to call for the punishment. Then he recited:
And [mention] when they said, "O God, if this is the truth from You, then rain down upon us stones from the sky or bring us a painful punishment"
[al-Anfāl: 32]. The correct reading in that is what the reciters of the major cities read, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

evidence.text: The reciters differed over the reading of that.
The general body of the reciters of the major cities read it: {taddaʿūn} with doubling of the dāl, meaning: taftaʿilūn ("you claim/call for"), from duʿāʾ.
And it is reported from Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk that they read it: (tadʿūn), meaning: you do [it] in this world (1).

Aḥmad b. Yūsuf told me, he said: al-Qāsim told us, he said: Ḥajjāj told us, from Hārūn, he said: Abān al-ʿAṭṭār and Saʿīd b. Abī ʿArūba informed us, from Qatāda, that he read it: (alladhī kuntum bihi tadʿūn) lightened, and said: They used to call for the punishment.
The correct reading in that is what the reciters of the major cities read, because of the consensus of the authoritative reciters on it.

x: Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Say, "Have you considered: whether God should destroy me and those with me or have mercy upon us, who can protect the disbelievers from a painful punishment?" (28)
The Exalted says to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: say, O Muḥammad, to the polytheists of your people:
h
Have you considered
, O people,
h
whether God should destroy me
and cause me to die,
h
and those with me, or have mercy upon us
and so delay our terms,
h
who can protect the disbelievers

in God from a painful, agonizing punishment? That is the punishment of the Fire. He says: our death and our life will not save the disbelievers from God's punishment; so you have no need to hasten the coming of the Hour and the descent of punishment, for that will not benefit you; rather it is a great trial for you.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Say, "He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him, and upon Him we have relied. And you will [soon] know who is in clear error" (29)
The Exalted says to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: say, O Muḥammad: our Lord is
h
the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him
. He says: we have affirmed Him,
h
and upon Him we have relied
. He says: and on Him we have depended in our affairs, and in Him we have placed our trust in them,
h
and you will [soon] know who is in clear error
. He says: you will know, O you who associate others with God, which of us and you is in deviation from the truth and is not on a straight road, when we come to Him and are all gathered.
Discussion of the interpretation of the saying of the Exalted:
h
Say, "Have you considered: if your water was to become sunken [into the earth], then who could bring you flowing water?" (30)
The Exalted says to His Prophet Muḥammad, may God bless him and grant him peace: say, O Muḥammad, to these polytheists:
h
Have you considered
, O people who set up equals to God,
h
if your water was to become sunken
. He says: sunk, so that buckets cannot reach it,
h
then who could bring you flowing (maʿīn) water?
. He says: who would come to you with flowing water. By maʿīn he means that which the eyes see as visible.
The interpreters said something like what we have said on this.
Mention of those who said that:

c: Muḥammad b. Saʿd told me, he said: My father related to me, he said: My uncle related to me, he said: My father related to me, from his father, from Ibn ʿAbbās
m: then who could bring you flowing water?

x: [ʿAbd al-Aʿlā]
n
b. Wāṣil told us, he said: ʿUbayd b. Hāshim
n
al-Bazzāz related to me, he said:

c: Sharīk told us, from Sālim, from Saʿīd b.
m: if your water was to become sunken
then who could bring you flowing water?

c: Bishr told us, he said: Yazīd told us, he said: Saʿīd told us, from Qatāda
m: Say, "Have you considered: if your water was to become sunken"
then who could bring you flowing water?
. He said: The maʿīn water is the running

x: I was told, from al-Ḥusayn, he said: I heard Abū Muʿādh say:

c: ʿUbayd told us, he said:
m: I heard al-Ḍaḥḥāk say regarding His saying:
then who could bring you flowing water?

x: It was said
h
ghawr
(sunken), describing the water by a verbal noun, as it is said: a night of ghamm
n
, meaning: a night that is overcast (ghāmma) (7).
End of the commentary on the sura "al-Mulk".

notes.en: Tafsīr Mujāhid p. 667; al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr 6/249 to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: تفسير مجاهد ص 667، وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 249 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Reported by ʿAbd al-Razzāq in his Tafsīr 2/306 from Maʿmar with it; al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr 6/249 to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.
notes.ar: أخرجه عبد الرزاق في تفسيره 2/ 306 عن معمر به. وعزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 249 إلى عبد بن حميد وابن المنذر.

notes.en: Mentioned by Abū Ḥayyān in al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ 8/303.
notes.ar: ذكره أبو حيان في البحر المحيط 8/ 303.

notes.en: Yaʿqūb, one of the Ten, read it so (al-Nashr 2/291). It was also read so by ʿIṣma from Abū Bakr, al-Aṣmaʿī from Nāfiʿ, Abū Rajāʾ, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Yasār ʿAbd Allāh b. Muslim, Sallām, Ibn Abī ʿAbla and Abū Zayd. See al-Baḥr al-Muḥīṭ 8/304.
notes.ar: وبها قرأ يعقوب من العشرة. النشر 2/ 291. وبها قرأ عصمة عن أبي بكر، والأصمعي عن نافع، وأبو رجاء والحسن وابن يسار عبد الله بن مسلم وسلام وابن أبي عبلة وأبو زيد. ينظر البحر المحيط 8/ 304.

notes.en: Attributed by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 6/249 to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 249 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: In M: "Ibn ʿAbd al-Aʿlā". It was given earlier in 8/96.
notes.ar: في م: "ابن عبد الأعلى". وتقدم في 8/ 96.

notes.en: In M: "Qāsim". See al-Jarḥ wa-l-Taʿdīl 6/5.
notes.ar: في م: "قاسم". وينظر الجرح والتعديل 6/ 5.

notes.en: Reported by al-Khaṭīb in Tārīkh Baghdād 14/403 via Sharīk with it.
notes.ar: أخرجه الخطيب في تاريخ بغداد 14/ 403 من طريق شريك به.

notes.en: Attributed by al-Suyūṭī in al-Durr al-Manthūr 6/249 to ʿAbd b. Ḥumayd.
notes.ar: عزاه السيوطي في الدر المنثور 6/ 249 إلى عبد بن حميد.

notes.en: Mentioned by al-Ṭūsī in al-Tibyān 10/72 and al-Qurṭubī in his Tafsīr 18/222.
notes.ar: ذكره الطوسي في التبيان 10/ 72، والقرطبي في تفسيره 18/ 222.

notes.en: In M: "ʿamm"; in T2, T3: "ghaym".
notes.ar: في م: "عم"، وفي ت 2، ت 3: "غيم".
